findings.claim: Removing the per-operation `AbortController` (`ac`) drops the only way this link could cancel an in-flight request when the observable is unsubscribed; any later `ac.abort()` in the teardown function will now reference an undefined variable (compile error), or the cancellation is silently lost.
findings.rationale: `ac` was created solely to be raced with `op.signal` and is almost certainly aborted in the returned teardown/unsubscribe callback further down the same `subscribe` body (outside this hunk). If that teardown was not also changed, this is a build break; if it was removed, unsubscribing no longer aborts the batched request, a real behavior change. High confidence this needs verification of the rest of the function.

findings.claim: Removing the `isDone` flag removes the guard that prevented aborting/cleaning up after the request had already settled.
findings.rationale: `isDone` was set to `true` in the `.then` handler, which only makes sense if read later (typically `if (!isDone) ac.abort()` in teardown). Deleting the declaration and assignment while keeping `_res` suggests the consumer must also have been removed; otherwise this is an undefined-variable reference. Worth confirming no remaining reader exists.

findings.claim: `loader.load(op)` now passes the caller's operation object by reference instead of a shallow copy, and relies entirely on `op.signal` for cancellation.
findings.rationale: Previously `{...op, signal: ...}` produced a fresh object so the dataloader/request builder could not mutate or retain the caller's operation, and cancellation worked even when the caller supplied no signal. Now, if `op.signal` is `undefined`, the request has no abort signal at all, and mutation/retention of `op` inside the loader leaks to the caller. Medium confidence this is intentional, but the loss of the copy is a subtle behavior change.

findings.claim: `raceAbortSignals` may now be an unused import in this file.
findings.rationale: This was the only call site shown; if no other usage remains, the import becomes dead and will fail lint / `noUnusedLocals` builds. Low-to-medium confidence since the file may use it elsewhere.
